acceptance: TestIcebergVacuum passes on windows-latest 3.12 in a dispatched nightly.yml run, or the owner records why a Windows run is not possible
A test shows a vacuum on a Windows-style location deletes only unreferenced files and keeps every referenced one
Linux and macOS vacuum behaviour is unchanged
context: Found by triage of the 2026-10-08 Windows 3.12 log (run 37776283388) during the nightly-red-issues batch. Split out of nightly-windows-teardown-and-singles-20261008 because a wrong fix could delete live data.
description: benchbox/platforms/dataframe/iceberg_maintenance.py: _local_table_dir (about line 457) calls urlparse on a plain Windows warehouse path such as C:\...\warehouse/default.db/probe and gets scheme 'c', so it returns None and vacuum reports metadata-only with 0 reclaimable files (tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_lakehouse_optimization.py TestIcebergVacuum, 2 tests, fail on windows-latest). _normalize_file_ref (about line 431) has the same drive-letter problem. Add one helper mapping a table or file location to a Path (single-letter scheme or no scheme -> Path(uri); file scheme -> Path(url2pathname(parsed.path)); anything else -> None) and use it in BOTH places. Fixing only _local_table_dir would make _reclaim_orphan_files treat live files as unreferenced and delete them, so both must change together. This path deletes files: confirm on a Windows run before merging.
